messages:
alex: hey team — onboarding hiccup: new hire tried the python sampleapp quickstart and the CLI never shows up after `pip install dist/sampleapp-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl` :confused:
alex: error is just `sh: 1: redwoodctl: not found` when they try to run the command. when installed in a venv the package imports fine though (`import sampleapp` works)
mira: do we define the console entry in pyproject? `[tool.poetry.scripts]` or `entry_points`?
alex: yep, pyproject has `redwoodctl = "sampleapp.cli:main"` under `[tool.poetry.scripts]` — wheel build prints it during `poetry build` but the installed wheel doesn't create the script
sam: could be a name/layout mismatch. is the package using `package = { include = "src/*" }` or a src layout? sometimes packaging tools mis-resolve when package name has a hyphen vs underscore
jordan: also check the top-level package folder name. If your package dir is `sample-app` but the module is `sampleapp` the wheel metadata can be weird. any logs from `pip install -v`?
alex: pasted the verbose bits: `Installing collected packages: sample-app` then `Successfully installed sample-app-0.1.0` but no console script entry. `pip install -v` output shows wheel METADATA with `Name: sample-app` and `Provides-Extra:` etc.
mira: aha — poetry's project.name can be `sample-app` while the importable module is `sampleapp`. That itself is fine, but `tool.poetry.scripts` uses the package import path, so still should wire the script. Could the wheel be built without the entry_points block?
sam: small repro I've seen: CI builds the wheel from a different pyproject (older), or there's a build backend hook that strips entry_points when using `poetry-core` + PEP 517 build isolation if `setup.cfg` exists. do you have any legacy setup files?
alex: repo has `setup.cfg` left over. removing it and rebuilding locally makes `redwoodctl` appear after `pip install dist/...whl`
jordan: yeah that can override metadata. weird edgecase: `python -m build` vs `poetry build` flip. which command do we recommend in quickstart?
mira: we should standardize on `poetry build` in docs and also add a CI check to assert console scripts exist in the wheel (inspect `dist/*.whl` for `entry_points.txt`)
sam: quick workaround for new hires: `pip install -e .` or `python -m pip install --force-reinstall dist/*.whl` after removing old egg-info — but editable fixes it because it uses local metadata, not wheel metadata
alex: new hire used `pipx install dist/sampleapp-0.1.0.whl` which silently created a package name mismatch and `pipx run redwoodctl` fails. `pipx list` showed `sample-app` but no bin
mira: pipx can be confusing with hyphens. For CLI tools we should recommend `pipx install sampleapp` from PyPI or `pipx install --spec path/to/wheel.whl` but add note about package name vs module name
jordan: unrelated but also saw `typing-extensions` pinned to 4.5 in the quickstart deps and our SDK's async client requires newer behavior; new hire hit `ImportError: cannot import name 'SomeProtocol' from typing_extensions` when running sampleapp async example
sam: that's because poetry.lock pinned transitive dep from another lib. run `pip check` to surface conflicts. maybe our sampleapp should declare `typing-extensions >= 4.6` explicitly in dev deps for compatibility with py3.11+
alex: action items: 1) remove legacy `setup.cfg` from template repos, 2) update quickstart docs to use `poetry build` and show `unpack wheel` check `unzip -p dist/*.whl '{distribution}/EGG-INFO/entry_points.txt'`, 3) add CI gate that installs wheel into a clean venv and asserts `which redwoodctl` exists, 4) pin/loosen typing-extensions in sampleapp dev deps
mira: +1. I'll open a small PR for the template and doc changes.
ci-bot: created issue RED-DEVEX-412: "sampleapp wheel missing console_scripts when setup.cfg present" and assigned to @mira
alex: thanks — saves at least one more onboarding call. :thumbsup:
mira: will post the PR link here when ready
sam: and I'll add a short checklist for new hires: `python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install dist/*.whl && which redwoodctl`
jordan: logging note: add a short troubleshooting snippet to onboarding doc showing `python -c "import pkg_resources;print(pkg_resources.get_entry_map('sample-app'))"` so folks can inspect entry points quickly
alex: perfect. closing for now, will follow up on the PR. :party_parrot:
